member.name: T:ClickWrap.InstalledApp
member.summary: Reads what the ClickWrap installer recorded about an installed app, and can hand off to that app's updater.
member.remarks: The installer writes these values under HKCU\Software\ClickWrap\{appId} after a successful install. An app runs from the ClickOnce store rather than its install folder, so this registration is how it finds its own update.exe.

member.name: M:ClickWrap.InstalledApp.GetCurrentVersion(System.String)
member.summary: The version to compare against the server: what the installer recorded, falling back to the entry assembly's version.
member.remarks: The registry value is preferred because it is the version actually pulled from the server, whereas a ClickOnce ApplicationVersion and an AssemblyVersion drift apart the moment one is bumped without the other — which would leave an app permanently convinced an update is available. The assembly version is the fallback for a build that was never installed through ClickWrap, such as one running from a developer machine.

member.name: M:ClickWrap.InstalledApp.StartUpdater(System.String)
member.summary: Starts this app's updater and leaves the app running, for when it needs to save state or close windows itself before exiting.
member.returns: false when there is no updater to start; the app is unaffected.

member.name: M:ClickWrap.InstalledApp.UpdateAndExit(System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: Starts this app's updater and immediately exits the app — the whole self-update in one call.
member.returns: false when there is no updater to start, leaving the app running. On success this does not return: the process ends.

remarks.para: The app must exit. setup.exe launches the app once it has updated it, so an app that stays open ends up running beside a second, newer copy of itself.
This exits the process directly, so unsaved state is not flushed and WPF's shutdown does not run. Use and close the app yourself when that matters.
